title: BACE: Biotechnology Skills (Practical) - Biotechnology Skills - Serial Dilutions
subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: A serial dilution is performed by adding 1 mL of sample to 9 mL of diluent. What is the dilution factor for this step?
questions.explain: Total volume = 1 + 9 = 10 mL. Dilution Factor = Sample Volume / Total Volume = 1 / 10.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: If you perform three consecutive 1:10 dilutions, what is the total dilution factor?
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: You count 45 colonies on a plate inoculated with 0.1 mL of a $10^{-4}$ dilution. What is the concentration of the original sample in CFU/mL?
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which plate count is considered statistically valid (countable)?
questions.explain: The standard countable range for petri plates is 30 to 300 colonies. 250 falls within this range.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What does TNTC stand for in microbiology?
questions.explain: TNTC means there are too many colonies (usually >300) to accurately count.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: You have a culture with $1 \times 10^8$ CFU/mL. You want to obtain a plate with approximately 100 colonies. If you plate 0.1 mL, what total dilution is required?
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Why do we perform serial dilutions instead of a single massive dilution?
options: It is more accurate to pipette 1 mL into 9 mL multiple times than to pipette 1 µL into 10 L once.
questions.explain: Pipetting extremely small volumes (like 1 µL) or managing huge volumes (like 1000 L) introduces large errors. Serial steps use manageable, accurate volumes.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: In a 1:5 dilution, 1 part of sample is mixed with how many parts of diluent?
questions.explain: A 1:5 dilution (1/5) means 1 part sample in a total volume of 5 parts. Diluent = Total - Sample = 5 - 1 = 4 parts.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: If you mix 100 µL of sample with 900 µL of broth, what is the dilution?
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which formula calculates the number of cells in the original stock from a dilution series?
questions.explain: Original Concentration = Colonies divided by the volume plated (to get per mL) and divided by the dilution factor (to correct for dilution). Mathematically equivalent to Colonies $\times$ Reciprocal of Dilution / Volume.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which diluent is most commonly used for bacterial serial dilutions to maintain cell viability?
questions.explain: PBS or saline is isotonic and prevents osmotic shock (bursting) of the cells. Pure water can cause lysis; ethanol and bleach kill cells.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.explain: CFU stands for Colony Forming Unit, assuming each colony arises from a single viable cell or clump of cells.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills
